summary: Support both session-cookie and bearer-JWT clients behind one authenticate_user. Cookie path for the browser (u1); JWT path for mobile (u2). Same local user store, no external IdP.

steps.title: Session cookie helpers
steps.description: Signed HttpOnly session cookie mapped to user_id in process memory.
steps.rationale: Honors u1 must: no external IdP, cookies for the browser.

steps.title: JWT issue and verify
steps.rationale: Honors u2 must: bearer JWT with 15-minute expiry.

steps.title: authenticate_user dispatcher
steps.description: def authenticate_user(request) -> User | None. Try session cookie, then Authorization: Bearer. Return None if both fail.
steps.rationale: Resolution of d1 and d2: one interface, two mechanisms, one owner.

steps.title: Login routes for both clients
steps.description: POST /login sets the session cookie AND returns {access_token, token_type, expires_in}. POST /logout clears the cookie. /health stays open.
steps.rationale: Resolution of d3: both response shapes, one endpoint.

resolutions.outcome: Both mechanisms ship. authenticate_user accepts a session cookie or a Bearer JWT.
resolutions.rationale: Each side's must-have is a client constraint, not a single-server constraint. Neither must was conceded.

resolutions.outcome: a1 writes src/auth/middleware.py. a2 does not touch it. jwt.py exports verify_access_token for the dispatcher to call.
resolutions.rationale: Same path cannot be owned by two parallel tickets.

resolutions.outcome: POST /login does both: Set-Cookie and a JSON token body.
resolutions.rationale: Minor; cheaper to satisfy both than to pick.
